title: Senior Center Sweep
style: country pop ballad, 92 BPM, acoustic guitar, lap steel, warm male vocal, gentle brushed drums, story-song narrative, nostalgic, humble, americana
lyrics:
[Intro]
Don't let the silver hair fool you, son
They been playing since before you were born

[Verse 1]
Walked in cocky, twenty-five and tall
Saw four grandparents waiting by the wall
Knee braces, visors, paddles taped up neat
Asked me politely if I wanted a seat

[Pre-Chorus]
First serve dropped like a feather on glass
Second one curved and it just walked past
By the third I was already learning
That my legs were the only thing burning

[Chorus]
Senior center sweep, eleven to two
Got educated by a lady named Sue
Senior center sweep, walk of shame
Lost to a man with a plastic knee and a soft soft game
Senior center sweep

[Verse 2]
He dinked me cross, he dinked me long
Hummed an old country song
Every ball came back like a letter from home
Politely returned, please leave me alone

[Pre-Chorus]
I tried to drive but I drove right out
She just smiled, didn't even shout
Patience is a paddle and they'd been holding it
Longer than I'd been alive on this planet

[Chorus]
Senior center sweep, eleven to two
Got educated by a lady named Sue
Senior center sweep, walk of shame
Lost to a man with a plastic knee and a soft soft game
Senior center sweep

[Bridge]
They invited me back for Tuesday at ten
I said yes ma'am, see you then

[Outro]
Don't let the silver hair fool you, son
They been playing since before you were born
